rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: an imperative or unclaimed heading inside a LECTURE blurs the grammar split that lets a declarative EXERCISE heading register as a law. Chunk 2 header 'The second loop' (L13) carries no verb and reads as subject-naming, the same shape as the rule's explicit catalogue-entry carve-out ('Ralph', 'The numbers') rather than a claim -- scored PASS under that carve-out. Chunk 5 header 'Keep your context where it loads optimally' (L38) is imperative-mood, structurally identical to the rule's own exercise example ('Read the ticket for your bug'), unlike this file's other declarative headers ('Rules have a ceiling', 'Prohibitions stop; taste steers'). It does not literally fit any of the three named NOT-violation shapes. Checked the maintainer block before scoring: raw L50 names this exact heading and its placement as a direct maintainer call ('The lecture closes on *Keep your context where it loads optimally* (Antti-directed 2026-08-23; reordered to last the same day so the live return is the final thing seen...)'), so the wording is authored intent, and the closer functions as the lecture's stated governing principle (a maxim in imperative clothing, akin to 'keep it simple') rather than a procedural instruction to perform an immediate task -- the actual task-shaped ask is the separate prompt fence two lines below (L44), not the header itself. Scored PASS rather than REVISE per the preamble's harm test and this class's own severity principle (a heading-grammar tell is not an 'I cannot follow this' failure). Filed as a TODO for the maintainer: the rule's NOT-violation list does not yet name 'closing principle phrased as a general practice' as a fourth shape alongside orientation/catalogue/phase-label, and this exact heading is a clean instance of it -- worth a carve-out if the pattern recurs on other module closers, so a future judge does not have to re-derive this reasoning per file.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Consider adding a fourth NOT-violation shape to rule 15 for maintainer-directed closer headings that function as a stated practice/maxim rather than a procedural instruction -- would remove the need for a per-file maintainer accept-note each time this pattern recurs.
